key_insight: Low DFT energy and force errors do not guarantee reliable disordered-carbon simulations; MACE-MH-1 was the most consistently robust foundation MLIP tested.
engineering_relevance: Application-specific validation can help engineers select reliable MLIPs for nanoporous carbon simulations, including more realistic oxygen- and hydrogen-containing structures.
method: Screen six foundation MLIPs using DFT energy and force errors and binding curves.
Test four models with melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics and structural analysis.
Evaluate pure and O/H-containing disordered carbons across phases, hybridisations and porous frameworks.
evidence_signal: Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories exposed failures missed by low DFT errors, while all four MD-tested models reproduced principal experimental and specialised-potential signatures of nanoporous carbon.
watch_item: Robustness is application-dependent: shared structural biases in OMAT-based models highlight training-coverage concerns despite differing architectures.
paper_title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
